$comment: THE RELEASE LEDGER. This file is the source of truth for what has shipped, and everything
else that states a version is checked against it by `node scripts/release.mjs --check`:
CHANGELOG.md is generated from it, apps/site/src/pages/changelog.astro must not advertise a
version it does not contain, and package.json may not declare one it has never heard of.
Newest first. Each entry's version must be what the entry below it BECOMES when these changes
ship — `kind` decides the bump, so the number follows the content rather than the other way
round. Kinds: added, changed, deprecated, removed, fixed, security, performance, internal.
`"breaking": true` on any change forces a major bump (demoted to a minor while major is 0).
The entries below were transcribed from the published changelog page, which was written by
hand and shipped before this ledger existed. They are the history as the product has already
announced it, not a reconstruction: every line here has a counterpart on that page.

releases.title: One model, measured
releases.lede: Every mode moved onto a single model, chosen by the eval suite rather than by taste — and the migration made the product both better and cheaper at once.

changes.text: Multi-model routing is gone. It existed to move cheap steps onto a smaller model; measurement showed that routing the post-inspection step made the outcome worse — the small model read the project tree and declared the task finished instead of building it.
Automatic retries, entirely. A retry is a second bill for the same work.
One engine now runs planning, building, memory and vision — 1M context, native tool calling, multimodal. Which engine that is stays an implementation detail chosen per step.
The gateway bills from the engine's own reported figure per call rather than from an estimate.
Sparks recalibrated: 1 Spark = 30 neurons, so a Spark stays a meaningful unit now that the same work costs less.
Four independent spend gates, each proven against production: a per-request ceiling, a daily ceiling, a monthly billable cap and an instant kill switch — all adjustable at runtime with no redeploy.
A full Agent build fell from $0.0139 to $0.0056 — 2.5x cheaper for the same work, on a model scoring 98.9 against 96.8 on the Roblox eval suite.

Leaner context: tool results capped at 3,000 characters and the agent transcript at 24,000, tool definitions filtered per mode, and step budgets tightened to 3 / 8 / 14 for Plan / Agent / Super Agent.

releases.title: First public release
releases.lede: The full describe-to-build loop: a web workspace, a real Studio plugin, and an agent that changes your actual place — carefully.

changes.text: Chat-driven building with live streaming responses and a visible tool trace — every get_project_tree, edit_script and run_and_check as it happens.
Three modes: Plan (2 Sparks), Agent (4 Sparks) and Super Agent (10 Sparks), which plans, builds, tests and fixes autonomously.
Unlimited projects per account, each with its own chat history and memory of what was built.
Image attachments, and a stop button that actually stops the agent mid-run.

The Studio plugin: pairing by short-lived code with a 10-minute expiry, script reading and editing through Studio's own editor APIs, typed instance operations, and a ChangeHistory waypoint around every batch so native undo works.
Run mode driven from the plugin — started, stopped, logged, and reported back for verification.
An automatic checkpoint before every agent run, manual checkpoints on demand, and one-click restore of scripts and instances across sessions.
The free tier: 60 Sparks per day as a hard quota that resets daily, with Pro on a waitlist.
